topics.title: Prices rose 5.54% in a year: is your savings account keeping up?
topics.angle: My money sits in a savings account or FD: after September's inflation figure, am I actually earning anything in real terms?
topics.why_now: MoSPI's September CPI (released 12 Oct 2026) jumped to 5.54% from 4.83%, food 7.74%; it also explains why RBI hiked on 7 Oct.

facts.label: All-India retail inflation (CPI, year on year), September
Food inflation (CFPI, year on year), September

verify: MoSPI press release of 12 Oct 2026 (base 2024=100) shows CPI 5.54% (provisional) and CFPI 7.74% for September 2026; August final 4.83%
Savings-account and FD rates are illustrative inputs stated as assumptions, never a named bank's rate
Real return = (1+nominal)/(1+inflation)-1, computed by code; do not call any product a loss-maker outright
Category differs from v-20261016-03 (emergency_fund, 'losing buying power'): tell a duel (savings account vs FD vs inflation), not the same erosion story

topics.title: Will paying by UPI above ₹2,000 cost you extra? What the new merchant fee really is
topics.angle: A shopkeeper refused my UPI payment over ₹2,000 / asked me to pay extra: is there a UPI charge now, and who pays it?
topics.why_now: NPCI's 0.4% merchant fee (MDR) on P2M UPI payments above ₹2,000 was due on 15 Oct and has been deferred until after Diwali; a niche Short on shopkeepers refusing UPI above ₹2,000 got ~40k views in its first 8 hours (market.json, 17 Oct).
verify: NPCI/Finance Ministry: MDR is charged to merchants, not customers; P2P transfers stay free
Proposed scope: 0.4% on P2M payments above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 from ₹75,000; small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month via QR exempt
Status on the day of the video: confirm whether the rollout is still deferred ('after Diwali', no notified date). If the reviewer can't confirm current status, fail the video
No on-screen figure as a sourced fact unless an official NPCI/PIB page with it is found; rate and threshold may appear only as spoken/explained inputs the reviewer confirms

topics.title: US prices up 3.7% in a year, energy up 20.4%: why your own inflation isn't the headline number
topics.angle: The news says 3.7%, but my gas and power bills feel much worse: what is my own inflation rate?
topics.why_now: BLS released September CPI on 14 Oct 2026: all items 3.7% over 12 months, energy 20.4%, core 2.6%. The Fed decides on 28 Oct, so inflation is the money story of the next two weeks in the US.

facts.label: US consumer prices, all items, change over 12 months to September
US energy prices, change over 12 months to September
US prices excluding food and energy, change over 12 months to September

verify: BLS CPI news release of 14 Oct 2026 (September 2026): all items +3.7% (12 months, not seasonally adjusted), energy +20.4%, all items less food and energy +2.6%, +0.6% for the month seasonally adjusted
A household's bills are illustrative inputs stated as assumptions (e.g. $250 a month on gas and power), never presented as an average
The extra yearly cost is computed by code (e.g. a lumpsum kind at 20.4% for 1 year on the yearly bill, or a price-rise kind if the improver adds one); do not say what prices will do next

topics.title: The Fed decides on 28 October: how a quarter point reaches your credit card bill
topics.angle: If the Fed moves rates, what changes on my credit card balance, and how fast?
topics.why_now: FOMC meets 27–28 Oct (decision 14:00 ET on 28 Oct); it raised the target range a quarter point to 3.75–4% on 16 Sep. Card APRs follow the prime rate, so a move shows up within a billing cycle or two. 9 days away: make it before the day.

facts.label: Upper end of the Fed's federal funds target range, set on 16 September

verify: Fed statement of 16 Sep 2026: target range raised by 1/4 point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent
Variable card APRs are typically the prime rate plus a margin, and prime usually moves with the Fed's range: explain in general terms, no named issuer
Card balance and APR (around 20–25%, channel profile) are illustrative inputs; the extra interest from +0.25 point is computed by code (card_min_due at two rates)
Say nothing about what the Fed will decide on 28 Oct

topics.title: The UK energy price cap is £1,723 a year, but it doesn't cap your bill
topics.angle: Ofgem says the cap is £1,723: does that mean I can't pay more than that this winter?
topics.why_now: Ofgem's cap rose 4% to £1,723 for a typical dual-fuel Direct Debit household from 1 Oct to 31 Dec 2026 (up £60 a year from £1,663), the highest in three years; UK outlets expect a further rise in January. Winter bills start now.

facts.label: Ofgem price cap, typical dual-fuel household paying by Direct Debit, a year, 1 October to 31 December
Rise in the cap for that household, a year
Previous cap for that household, a year

verify: Ofgem press release of 26 Aug 2026: cap rises £60 a year (£5 a month) to £1,723 for 1 Oct–31 Dec 2026; current cap £1,663
The cap limits unit rates and standing charges, not the total bill: a household using more than typical pays more than £1,723
Usage figures are illustrative assumptions; the cost of using more is computed by code. No supplier or tariff named or recommended
Do not state the January cap: it is only a forecast until Ofgem announces it

topics.title: Social Security's 3.6% raise for 2027: how it's worked out and what it means per month
topics.angle: Social Security checks go up 3.6% in January: where does that number come from, and what does it add up to over a year?
topics.why_now: SSA announced the 2027 COLA on 14 Oct 2026: 3.6%, the largest in years (2026 was 2.8%), for nearly 72 million beneficiaries from January. It is tied to the CPI-W, a different index from the 3.7% headline CPI the channel already covered.

facts.label: Social Security cost-of-living adjustment for 2027
Average rise in a Social Security retirement benefit, a month

verify: SSA release of 14 Oct 2026: 3.6% COLA from January 2027 for nearly 72 million beneficiaries; SSI increases from 31 Dec 2026; average retirement benefit up about $75 a month
The COLA follows the CPI-W (Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers), not the headline CPI-U; don't call one a loss against the other
No advice on when to claim benefits; the yearly total is computed by code

ECB deposit facility rate before the September rise

topics.title: UK card rules: what your card company must do after 18 and 36 months of mostly paying interest
topics.angle: I only ever pay the minimum on my card. Is there a point where the bank has to step in?
topics.why_now: Credit card debt is the most active search in this week's market data (Martin Lewis's card-debt alert Short, 12.9k views in 2 days; 9 of the top 30 niche Shorts are on card debt), and no UK card story has run yet.
verify: FCA persistent-debt rules (PS18/4): 'persistent debt' means paying more in interest, fees and charges than off the balance over 18 months; firms must contact the customer at 18 months and, at 36 months, offer a way to repay in a reasonable period
Card balance, APR (~20-25% UK) and payments are illustrative; interest and the 18-month split are computed by code (card_min_due, GBP)
Don't name a card, lender or balance-transfer deal; free debt help (StepChange, National Debtline, Citizens Advice) may be named
